title: United bars unauthorized AI agents from booking its flights. OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly tops $10 billion, still at a loss. Google’s Decisions API answers 1,000 questions in one call, and AWS ships a free local emulator. Databricks’ Genie works in the background. DeepMind proves Signal’s code secure. Stolen AI keys cost Railway customers $740,000, and 35,000 Grok Build apps were left open.
summary: United Airlines said on 11 November that unauthorized AI agents may not book, change or check in for its flights, even with the customer’s permission, and that travel agencies need its approval to use AI tools. TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reported OpenAI’s third-quarter revenue passed $10 billion, up from $6.7 billion, with its operating margin improving from minus 150 to minus 109 percent. Google launched the Gemini Decisions API, which scores up to 1,000 yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one call for $0.10 per million input tokens. AWS released AWS Emulator, a free local stand-in for its APIs built by AI agents, which does not check IAM permissions. Databricks announced an always-on Genie that works in the background and emails people for decisions, coming to preview. Google DeepMind’s AlphaProof Code proved key security properties of Signal’s compiled code in four weeks. Railway said an attacker hunting AI keys could have decrypted secrets in up to 100,000 workspaces, with about $740,000 in unauthorized charges. Claroc found about 35,000 Grok Build apps open to anyone through public DNS records.
uncertainty: United’s policy details are from its own help page; how it will enforce the block is not described. OpenAI’s revenue and margin figures come from Bloomberg’s and the WSJ’s anonymous sources as reported by TechCrunch and Reuters, not from OpenAI. The Decisions API speed, price comparison and benchmark claims are Google’s. AWS Emulator’s description and limits are AWS’s. Databricks’ always-on Genie is announced, not yet in preview; Ghodsi’s demo is TechCrunch’s account. AlphaProof Code results are DeepMind’s, with Signal’s CTO quoted; the proofs cover the specified properties only. Railway’s 100,000 workspace figure is its own upper bound and the $740,000 is its estimate. Grok Build figures are Claroc’s as reported by Ars Technica; Cursor disputes the default setting.

stories.theme: United Airlines now bars unauthorized AI agents from booking, changing or checking in for its flights, including through travel agencies
stories.changed: On Wednesday 11 November 2026 United Airlines published a policy that restricts unauthorized third-party AI agents and assistants. United says it is taking steps to restrict them directly on its website and app and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators. Its help page says that if an agent, bot, browser extension or browser feature searches, books, buys, manages or collects information on united.com or the United app without United’s permission, it is unauthorized. Giving an agent your own permission does not change that. United says agents risk exposing personal information or making bookings, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles without the traveller’s approval. It also says automatic check-in by an agent could break FAA and DOT rules, because check-in needs a person to confirm that bags do not contain banned items such as explosives. Bookings made by agents before 11 November will not be cancelled. Travel agencies may use their own AI tools only with United’s permission. You can still use AI to research trips, as long as the tool does not touch United’s site or app, and assistive technology for disabled customers is not affected. United says it does not work with any third-party AI agents yet. CNBC notes that Amazon has blocked Meta’s Muse agent, while Walmart has partnered with it.
stories.matters: This is one of the first big consumer brands to write down, in public, that a customer’s own AI agent may not act for them. Agents that book and buy only work if the sites let them in.
stories.imply: Do not assume an agent that can book a flight is allowed to. Do not hand an agent your loyalty login to get round the rule. United says that is exactly what puts miles and bookings at risk.
uses: If you book work travel with an AI assistant, use it to compare United flights, then buy on united.com or the United app yourself.
If you ever gave an agent your MileagePlus login, change the password now, as United advises.
If you run a travel desk or agency, check whether any of your tools use AI agents on United’s channels. United now requires its permission.
stories.example: An office manager asks her AI assistant to find the cheapest United fare for a Chicago trip. It lists three options. She opens the United app, books the one she picked, and checks in herself, confirming the bag declaration.
stories.audience: Business travellers, travel managers, travel agencies, and anyone building shopping or booking agents.
stories.watch: Whether United approves any agent integrations, and on what terms. Whether other airlines follow. How OpenAI and Meta respond for their booking agents. Not a new model.

source.title: United Airlines: Unauthorized third-party AI agents or assistants, 11 November 2026
source.quote: Just because you’ve given access to AI assistants doesn’t mean United will permit an AI assistant to transact with United.

stories.theme: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly passed $10 billion for the first time, up from $6.7 billion, while it still loses money on each sale
stories.changed: On Wednesday 11 November 2026 TechCrunch reported, citing Bloomberg and its anonymous sources, that OpenAI’s revenue crossed $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026 for the first time. TechCrunch says that would be an almost 50 percent jump from the $6.7 billion OpenAI reportedly made in the second quarter, when growth from the first quarter’s $5.7 billion was about 18 percent. The report says OpenAI’s adjusted operating margin narrowed from minus 150 percent in the second quarter to minus 109 percent in the third, which means it still spent more to run the business than it earned. Bloomberg puts OpenAI’s annual revenue run rate at $50 billion. Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, also reported revenue rising to $10 billion alongside steep losses. TechCrunch credits tighter pricing, discounts, better models and more products for businesses and agents. For comparison, TechCrunch notes Anthropic recently reported third-quarter revenue of $17 billion and an $81 billion run rate at the end of October, and that the two companies count partner sales differently. OpenAI has not published these figures itself.
stories.matters: It is the clearest sign yet that OpenAI’s business sales are picking up, and that it still pays heavily for every dollar it earns. That affects how long today’s prices and discounts can last.
stories.imply: Do not treat these as official results. They come from anonymous sources, and OpenAI is private. Do not compare OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s run rates as if they were measured the same way. TechCrunch says they are not.
uses: If you are negotiating an OpenAI contract, ask for prices locked for the full term. A company with a reported operating margin of minus 109 percent may tighten discounts.
Use the minus 150 to minus 109 percent margin change to explain to finance why AI prices may rise rather than fall.
When you compare vendors, ask each for its own revenue counting method before quoting run rates side by side.
stories.example: A procurement lead renewing a ChatGPT Enterprise deal reads the report. She asks OpenAI for a two-year price lock and a cap on yearly increases, noting in her memo that the figures are unconfirmed press reports.
stories.audience: Finance and procurement teams, investors, and companies that buy from OpenAI.
stories.watch: Whether OpenAI confirms the numbers. Whether its margin keeps narrowing. Whether discounts shrink at renewals. Not a new model.

source.title: TechCrunch: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time, 11 November 2026
source.quote: OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said.

stories.theme: Google’s new Gemini Decisions API answers up to 1,000 yes/no, choice and scoring questions in one call, for $0.10 per million input tokens
stories.changed: On Wednesday 11 November 2026 Google launched the Gemini Decisions API, run by a new model called Gemini Decision 1, in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. It does not write text. You send it one input, which can mix text, images, audio, video and PDFs up to 256,000 tokens, plus up to 1,000 separate questions. Each question is a yes/no check, a multiple choice of 2 to 255 options, or a score on a rubric you define. It scores the options in a single pass and returns a probability and a confidence score from 0 to 1 for each answer, so your code can send unclear cases to a person. Google says it takes 150 to 250 milliseconds end to end and costs $0.10 per million input tokens, with no charge for output. The shared input is billed once per request, however many questions you ask. Google says it is nearly 5 times cheaper across its benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and that it leads its benchmarks with the lowest calibration error. Gemini Notebook uses it to route questions to the right model, which Google says cut latency by up to 40 percent for everyday queries. There is a no-cost tier for prototyping.
stories.matters: Many agent and workflow steps are small judgments: which queue, is anything missing, how urgent. This makes those steps fast and cheap, and tells you how sure the model is.
stories.imply: Do not use it for tasks that need written answers. It only picks from options you give it. Do not trust the confidence score blindly. Test it on your own cases before letting it route anything without review.
uses: Triage incoming support emails into queues, with low-confidence ones sent to a person.
Check an expense claim’s receipt photo and form against your policy questions in one call.
Pick which model should answer each request, the way Google’s own Gemini Notebook does.
stories.example: A claims team sends one request with a scanned claim form and three damage photos. It asks: is any document missing, which team should handle it, and how urgent is it from 0 to 3. Claims scored below 0.8 confidence go to a reviewer.
stories.audience: Developers building agents and workflows, and operations teams that sort, check or route high volumes of items.
stories.watch: Independent accuracy tests. Rival products, which VentureBeat says include OpenAI’s own Decisions API. Support in Gemini on Google Cloud, which Google says is coming soon.

source.title: Google: Gemini Decisions API, fast, calibrated multimodal decisions, 11 November 2026
source.quote: Your shared input is billed once per request no matter how many questions you evaluate (each question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens).

stories.theme: AWS released a free local copy of its cloud APIs for testing on your laptop, written and maintained by AI agents
stories.changed: On Wednesday 11 November 2026 Amazon Web Services made AWS Emulator generally available. It runs on your own computer and answers the same AWS API calls as the cloud, so the AWS command line, the AWS SDKs and coding agents such as Kiro or Claude Code can create and test resources like DynamoDB tables or S3 buckets without deploying to AWS. It has no service fee and its source is on GitHub. It installs from RPM or Debian packages on Linux and runs in Docker on macOS and Windows. AWS says it supports services that have a published API model and is built from the same models the SDKs use. AWS says the emulator is built and maintained by agents: one group finds gaps against real AWS, another writes tests and fixes, and an independent security agent reviews changes before release. AWS publishes a fidelity score for each service, showing how many of its tests match real AWS. AWS lists clear limits. It does not check IAM permissions the way AWS does, so a request AWS would deny may succeed. Each emulator acts as one account, with no cross-account or cross-Region behaviour. It sends anonymous usage data by default, which you can turn off. Unsupported operations return an error straight away.
stories.matters: Testing against the real cloud is slow and costs money every time. A free local stand-in lets developers and their coding agents try changes in seconds.
stories.imply: Do not use it to test security. AWS says it does not evaluate IAM policies. Do not assume a test that passes locally will pass on AWS. Check the fidelity score for each service you use.
uses: Point your existing unit tests at the emulator so they run without an AWS account or a deploy.
Let a coding agent build and retry DynamoDB or S3 code locally before it touches your real account.
Turn off the anonymous usage data if company policy requires it.
stories.example: A developer asks Claude Code to add a DynamoDB cache to a service. The agent creates the table, writes and reads items against AWS Emulator on her laptop, and only after the tests pass does she deploy to a staging account on AWS.
stories.audience: Cloud developers, platform teams, and anyone running coding agents against AWS.
stories.watch: Fidelity scores for the services you rely on. Whether IAM checks are added. How it compares with LocalStack. Not a new model.

source.title: AWS News Blog: Test your applications against AWS locally with AWS Emulator, 11 November 2026
source.quote: It doesn’t evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and resource-based policies the way AWS does, so a request that AWS denies might succeed in the emulator.

stories.theme: Databricks turned Genie into an always-on agent that runs work in the background and emails you when it needs a decision
stories.changed: On Wednesday 11 November 2026 Databricks announced the second generation of Genie, its AI assistant for business data. Databricks says you give Genie a goal and clear limits, and it runs in the background on its own compute, hands parts of the job to sub-agents, tracks progress, chases missing inputs, and contacts you when a person needs to decide. A new priority inbox shows what needs attention, and each alert arrives as its own email thread. Every action stays within Unity Catalog permissions and Unity Gateway approval rules and budgets, and is logged. Genie Ontology, which records a company’s metric definitions, people and processes, is now generally available. Genie Search will cover more than 100 data sources, including Google Drive, Jira and Confluence. Genie is priced on usage, not per seat. Databricks says Genie and Genie Ontology are generally available now, while the always-on Genie, Genie Search and Ontology Manager are coming soon to preview and beta. In a TechCrunch demo, chief executive Ali Ghodsi showed Genie analysing weak scores in an employee survey and summarising a sales pitch that went badly.
stories.matters: Office AI is moving from answering when asked to working unasked in the background. That shifts the job from writing prompts to setting goals, limits and budgets.
stories.imply: Do not plan on the always-on version yet. It is not generally available. Do not let a background agent run without spending caps and approval rules in place first.
uses: If you are on Databricks, set up Genie Ontology now with your official definitions of revenue and other key metrics. The always-on agent will rely on them.
Write down a goal, limits and a budget for one repeat job, such as a weekly revenue brief, ready to test in the beta.
Ask your admin to set per-team spending limits in Unity Gateway before anyone turns on background work.
stories.example: A customer success lead plans to ask Genie to watch usage for her top 50 accounts and email the account team when one drops sharply. She first agrees with data engineering how usage is defined in Genie Ontology.
stories.audience: Databricks customers, data teams, and managers who want routine reporting done for them.
stories.watch: When the always-on Genie reaches preview and then general availability. Real costs per task. How well approval rules hold up. Not a new model.

source.title: Databricks: Databricks launches new always-on Genie, autonomous AI for complex enterprise work, 11 November 2026
source.quote: Genie and Genie Ontology are generally available to all customers. Genie Search, Ontology Manager and the new always-on Genie are coming soon to preview and beta programs.

stories.theme: Google DeepMind used AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of Signal’s actual code, in four weeks
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a system in which human experts and AI agents work together to formally verify software, meaning to prove mathematically that code does what it is meant to. DeepMind says researchers and models first turned Signal’s security goals into formal specifications, with human experts reviewing every one. Agents running on Gemini Carbon then wrote the proofs, more than six million lines in Lean, a language whose checker confirms each proof. The agents flagged about 1 percent of the work for a person to review. DeepMind says the proofs cover the compiled code that runs on devices, not only the design, including properties such as keeping messages protected before and after a device is briefly compromised. The work took four weeks, which DeepMind says historically takes expert teams years. To test it, the team put two real, previously fixed bugs back into an isolated copy of Signal’s code, and in both cases the system proved the buggy version insecure. Signal’s chief technology officer, Ehren Kret, called it a major breakthrough. DeepMind is open-sourcing the verification artifacts. The proofs cover the properties the experts specified, not every part of Signal or every possible attack.
stories.matters: Proving code correct has been too slow and costly for most software. If AI makes it weeks instead of years, the strongest level of security checking could reach the software businesses depend on.
stories.imply: Do not read this as Signal being impossible to hack. It proves the specified properties of the core code. Do not expect this for your own code tomorrow. DeepMind says scaling it needs more research.
uses: Security teams can read the open-sourced artifacts to see what a machine-checked specification for real code looks like.
When you assess a messaging tool for staff, ask whether its protocol code has been formally verified, not just reviewed.
Use the two reintroduced bugs as an example when asking any AI security vendor how it proves its tool catches real flaws.
stories.example: A CISO choosing a secure messaging app for executives adds a question to the vendor form: has the protocol implementation been formally verified, by whom, and which properties were proved? She cites Signal’s work with DeepMind as the benchmark.
stories.audience: Security teams, software leaders, and anyone choosing tools for sensitive communication.
stories.watch: Whether outside experts check the proofs. Whether it is applied to other protocols, firmware or grid software, as DeepMind suggests. Not a new model.

source.title: Google DeepMind: Introducing AlphaProof Code, a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth, 10 November 2026
source.quote: Even at this complexity, our verification process took just four weeks – a task that historically takes expert teams years – proving that Signal's core cryptographic code delivers the security protections our experts specified.

stories.theme: Railway says an attacker hunting for AI keys decrypted secrets from up to 100,000 workspaces and ran up about $740,000 in charges
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Railway, a cloud platform for deploying apps, published its full report on an attack between 20 and 21 October. Railway says the attacker escaped part of its build isolation, stole an internal credential, copied Railway’s own code, then used a misconfigured cloud login setting to reach a credential that could decrypt customer environment variables. Its database logs show the attacker searching specifically for AI provider keys and targeting customers with many variables. Railway says at most 1.85 percent of workspaces, about 100,000, could have had variables decrypted, and calls that an upper bound. Linked-account tokens for 1,852 users were also taken and reset. Railway estimates unauthorized spending on the stolen keys at about $740,000. It believes the keys were sold to services that resell AI access for distillation, and notes that OpenCode, Warp, Fireworks AI and others disclosed similar thefts between 6 and 23 October. AWS Bedrock and Google are refunding fraud, OpenAI and SpaceXSI review cases, and Railway says it will cover costs that providers such as OpenRouter will not refund, and is covering Anthropic costs for now. Each weakness used has been fixed, it says.
stories.matters: Stolen AI keys turn straight into money, so attackers now hunt for them on the platforms that store them. Your AI bill can be run up by someone else.
stories.imply: Do not keep AI keys with no spending cap. Do not assume a hosting platform’s encryption keeps secrets safe if the platform itself is breached.
uses: If you used Railway in October, rotate every AI, cloud, database and payment key stored there, and report unexpected charges through Railway’s form.
Set monthly spending limits and usage alerts on every AI provider key, wherever it is stored.
Give each app its own AI key so one theft can be traced and revoked without breaking everything.
stories.example: A startup CTO sees a spike on the company’s OpenAI bill from late October. She rotates the key stored in Railway, opens an OpenAI support case, passes the case ID to Railway support, and sets a hard monthly cap on the new key.
stories.audience: Developers, startup founders, and IT teams who store AI keys on hosting platforms.
stories.watch: Whether Anthropic agrees refunds. The outside forensic firm’s findings. More platforms reporting the same kind of key theft. Not a new model.

source.title: Railway: Incident report, October 21st security attack, 10 November 2026
source.quote: Database logs show that the attacker was specifically prioritizing AI provider keys in their queries by selecting rows where the variable name matched attacker-provided regular expressions.

stories.theme: About 35,000 apps made with Grok Build were open to anyone, because their share links could be found through public DNS records
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Ars Technica reported research by the security firm Claroc into Grok Build, the app-building agent from SpaceXSI, the merged SpaceX and xAI. Grok Build gives each shared app its own web address made of random words, such as cinder-crane-sand-frost.grok.me. Because the random part sits in the domain name, the addresses show up in passive DNS databases that anyone can search. Claroc found 43,601 grok.me addresses, and more than 35,000 of them, nearly 95 percent, opened the app and its data with no sign-in. Claroc said its tests showed links were set to Anyone with the link by default. A representative for Cursor, which SpaceXSI acquired, said apps are private by default. Exposed data included 3,784 worker medical exams at a construction company, a hospital roster of about 3,565 staff, a Navy contractor roster, and 24 of SpaceXSI’s own apps, including a confidential sales onboarding plan and a map of 594 sales accounts. SpaceXSI removed its own apps after Ars asked about them, while most other data was still reachable when the story ran. Claroc says Lovable, Bolt and Replit also give each app its own address, so the same records expose them.
stories.matters: Staff are building internal tools with AI in minutes, and putting real company data in them. A share link is not a password if anyone can list it.
stories.imply: Do not treat an unguessable-looking link as private. Do not let staff put personal or confidential data into AI-built apps without sign-in protection.
uses: If anyone at your company uses Grok Build, switch every shared app to invited users or only you today.
Ask teams to list any internal apps made with Grok Build, Lovable, Bolt or Replit, and check which hold personal data.
Add AI app builders to your data policy: real customer or staff data only behind company sign-in.
stories.example: An HR lead learns a colleague built a staff training tracker with Grok Build and shared it by link. She changes the sharing to invited users, moves the employee IDs out of the app, and asks IT to check for others.
stories.audience: IT and security teams, HR and operations staff who build their own tools, and anyone using AI app builders.
stories.watch: Whether SpaceXSI changes the link design and default setting, and tells affected users. Whether other app builders move the random part out of the domain. Not a new model.

AWS, 11 Nov: AWS Emulator GA; free; local HTTPS endpoint for CLI/SDKs/agents; built and maintained by agents; per-service fidelity scores; no IAM evaluation; single account; telemetry on by default. Not a new model.

Databricks, 11 Nov: second-generation always-on Genie (sub-agents, priority inbox, email alerts, Unity Gateway budgets); Genie and Genie Ontology GA; always-on Genie, Genie Search, Ontology Manager coming to preview/beta. Not a new model.

Google DeepMind, 10 Nov: AlphaProof Code verified key security properties of Signal’s compiled code; 6M+ lines of Lean by Gemini Carbon agents; ~1% flagged for human review; four weeks; two reintroduced bugs caught. Not a new model.

Railway, 10 Nov: 20–21 Oct attack targeted AI keys; up to 1.85% (~100,000) workspaces could have had variables decrypted; 1,852 users’ linked tokens reset; ~$740,000 unauthorized spend; Railway covers unrefunded charges. Not a new model.
